status: Steps 02–08 documentation prepared; application implementation not started
persona_note: Fictional planning personas. Names, images and situations are assumptions, not user research. Stable IDs are for project documentation, not application role names.

personas.name: Maya
personas.context: Maya prepares recordings that her course team owns. She has a folder of clips ready for processing.
personas.goal: Submit the folder once, see each result, retry failures and check playback.
personas.pain: Separate upload and conversion tools require repeated manual work. A failed encode can interrupt the preparation task.
needs: One result per submitted file, including readable failures.
A retry that uses the stored source.
personas.success: The batch reports every file. Successful outputs play. Failed jobs can be retried without another upload.
personas.boundary: Maya’s account owns her uploads. The demo does not model shared team ownership, student access or an LMS.

personas.name: Arun
personas.context: Arun creates his own short training videos. He submits and checks one video through the browser.
personas.goal: Upload a video, follow its status and watch the processed result.
personas.pain: Video formats vary. Conversion takes time. An unclear failure leaves him unsure what to do next.
needs: A supported video upload with clear input errors.
Visible queued, processing, done or failed status.
Playable MP4 output and best-effort HLS.
personas.success: His video becomes playable, or a visible failure offers a stored-source retry. Another owner cannot access it.
personas.boundary: Arun reviews his own output. This does not create a public channel, sharing settings, search or analytics.

personas.name: Jules
personas.channel: Published API and Publisher CLI source
personas.context: Jules adds video preparation to a content tool. The Publisher CLI is the project’s concrete example of that integration.
personas.goal: Use the published API without copying the service implementation.
personas.pain: Each application otherwise needs storage, processing, status and access-control integration.
needs: A reference client with no database credentials or service imports.
personas.success: The CLI completes the same workflow through the API. Its implementation effort and size can be recorded.
personas.boundary: Jules does not require a developer portal, tenant system, API billing or a third application.

personas.name: Sam
personas.context: Sam operates the demonstration platform. Backlogs and new releases require changes to processing capacity and software versions.
personas.goal: Change worker capacity and release Processing while keeping Media Management unchanged.
personas.pain: A coupled release can disturb the user-facing application. Unclear job failures make recovery difficult to check.
needs: Visible job outcomes and recovery behavior.
Independent worker scaling with recorded resources.
A versioned release, smoke test and rollback path.
personas.success: Scaling and release experiments produce traceable results. A Processing release passes its smoke test and can be rolled back.
personas.boundary: Sam is an operator persona, not a new product administrator feature. The scope excludes an operations dashboard and an autoscaler.

use_cases.name: Register, log in and upload an owned video
use_cases.actors: Maya / Arun. Jules integrates the API.
use_cases.before: The person owns the demonstration content. Registration or login establishes the caller.
use_cases.story: As a content owner, I want to submit a supported video so that I can prepare it for playback.
acceptance: A valid authenticated upload of at most 100 MiB records the caller as owner and starts asynchronous work.
The client receives a reference it can use to track the submitted item.
The platform rejects anonymous, unsupported and oversized uploads.
use_cases.evidence: Owned upload result plus anonymous, invalid-type and oversized rejection cases.
use_cases.source: P2 §2.3 and UC-1. P1 §4.1–4.2 supplies background.

use_cases.name: Process video into playable outputs
use_cases.before: The platform accepted a valid source.
use_cases.story: As a content owner, I want compatible outputs without manually running a converter.
acceptance: A successful job provides MP4 output.
Suitable sources produce best-effort HLS at the supported ladder heights. HLS failure can retain the MP4 fallback.
A processing failure leaves a visible failure state rather than an indefinite success claim.
use_cases.evidence: Source and job reference, state history, MP4 playback and HLS/fallback evidence.

use_cases.name: Track status and access playback
use_cases.before: The caller owns the submitted item.
use_cases.story: As an owner, I want to see the processing result and check the resulting video.
acceptance: The owner can retrieve queued, processing, done or failed status.
The browser plays the completed output. The CLI reports status and provides authorised output access.
Another owner cannot retrieve that item’s status or playback access through the API.
use_cases.evidence: Owner status, browser playback, CLI output and cross-owner rejection.

use_cases.name: Retry from the stored source
use_cases.before: The caller owns a failed job and its source remains available.
use_cases.story: As an owner, I want to retry a failed encode without transferring the same video again.
acceptance: An authorised retry uses the existing source. The browser must not upload its remembered file again.
Only a failed job is eligible. The platform rejects other states and other owners.
The retry has a visible result. Attempts must not create unintended duplicate outputs.
use_cases.evidence: Failed-to-retry workflow, unchanged source, no re-upload, rejection cases and output check.
use_cases.source: P2 §2.3, UC-4, §3.4. Current gap: frontend/app.js lines 410–412.

use_cases.name: Bulk-publish a folder and report results
use_cases.before: Maya has credentials and a folder of team-owned demonstration videos.
use_cases.story: As a course coordinator, I want a batch command so that I avoid repeating the same web upload task.
acceptance: The CLI submits the folder through the published API and reports each file’s outcome.
Failures remain visible in the batch result. This planning choice prevents a single success message from hiding failed files.
The client uses no service-code imports and no database credentials.
use_cases.evidence: CLI command, per-file results, dependency review and actual implementation effort.
use_cases.source: P2 §1.3, UC-5, §3.3–3.4. Per-file failure visibility is the chosen business acceptance interpretation.

use_cases.name: Scale processing capacity independently
use_cases.before: A fixed test backlog and enough host capacity are available.
use_cases.story: As an operator, I want to change worker capacity without changing the user-facing service.
acceptance: Worker count changes from one to two to three without scaling or redeploying Media Management.
The planned comparison uses thirty identical 60-second 720p clips and two vCPU per worker.
Results record throughput, queue wait, processing time, failures, CPU and memory against the proposal targets.
use_cases.evidence: Worker configurations, unchanged Media Management version and the scaling results.

use_cases.name: Release Processing and demonstrate rollback
use_cases.before: A previous Processing image and a new candidate image exist.
use_cases.story: As an operator, I want a separate Processing release so that I can change it without releasing Media Management.
acceptance: The pipeline deploys the new version and runs an upload-to-playback smoke test.
The Media Management container and media_db migrations remain unchanged.
The release can return to the previous image. The initial release-plus-smoke target remains at most ten minutes.
use_cases.evidence: Image references, release timing, smoke output, unchanged components and rollback result.

business_decisions.decision: Focus the demonstration on owned training content
business_decisions.reason: Use course recordings and independent training clips as concrete examples of the small content teams in the proposals.

business_decisions.decision: Treat the authenticated uploader as the owner
business_decisions.reason: “Course team” is a business setting. It does not introduce organisations, shared ownership or team accounts.

business_decisions.decision: Use the owner as the demonstrated viewer
business_decisions.reason: Maya and Arun consume their own outputs. A separate learner-access or sharing system is outside this scope.

business_decisions.decision: Define publishing as preparing owner-accessible outputs
business_decisions.reason: The CLI does not make a video public, publish to an LMS or distribute it to students.

business_decisions.decision: Keep the web app and CLI as the two clients
business_decisions.reason: The CLI demonstrates reuse. No developer portal or third application is needed.

business_decisions.decision: Keep UC-1 through UC-7 and all proposal quality targets
business_decisions.reason: These acceptance stories clarify the submitted scope. They do not replace its numeric targets.

business_decisions.decision: Carry the boundary question into step 03
business_decisions.reason: Two services remain the proposal direction. Detailed DDD must test their suitability before implementation.
